title: Notation
body_md:
lowercase and uppercase boldface letters
denote vectors and matrices; $(\cdot)^T$, $(\cdot)^H$, and
$(\cdot)^\dagger$ denote transpose, Hermitian transpose, and
pseudoinverse; $\operatorname{diag}(\cdot)$ is a diagonal matrix; $\Re\{\cdot\}$ is
the real part; $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm; $\bm e_n$ is the
$n$-th column of $\bm I_N$; $\bm 1_K$ is the all-ones vector; and
$\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$ are the real and complex fields.

label: eq:ar2
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\varphi_m=\omega_omT_s+\nu_0$ and $\Delta_o=\omega_oT_s$. By the
sum identities for sine and cosine,
$\bm r_s[m+1]+\bm r_s[m-1]
=
R_o\bm p_o\!\left[\cos(\varphi_m+\Delta_o)+\cos(\varphi_m-\Delta_o)\right]
+
R_o\bm q_o\!\left[\sin(\varphi_m+\Delta_o)+\sin(\varphi_m-\Delta_o)\right]
=
2\cos(\Delta_o)\bm r_s[m]$.

label: eq:update
title: Proposition
body_md:
For $\eta>0$, \eqref{eq:LS} is strictly convex and has the unique
solution
 
\begin{equation}
\Delta\bm\theta^\star[m]
=
-
(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T
\left[
\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+
(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T
+
\eta\bm I_K
\right]^{-1}
\overline{\bm b}[m].
\label{eq:update}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: One-shot multilayer update

title: Proof
body_md:
The objective of \eqref{eq:LS} is a quadratic whose Hessian,
$2[(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+
+\eta\bm I_{LN}]$, satisfies
$\bm x^T[(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+
+\eta\bm I_{LN}]\bm x
=\left\lVert \overline{\bm J}_\theta^+\bm x\right\rVert_2^2+\eta\left\lVert \bm x\right\rVert_2^2>0$
for every $\bm x\neq\bm 0$ and $\eta>0$. Hence \eqref{eq:LS} is
strictly convex and its unique minimizer solves the stationarity
condition $
\left[
(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+
+\eta\bm I_{LN}
\right]\Delta\bm\theta^\star
=
-(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T\overline{\bm b}$. Since $(\bm A^T\bm A+\eta\bm I_{LN})\bm A^T
=\bm A^T(\bm A\bm A^T+\eta\bm I_K)$ for any
$\bm A\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times LN}$, with both parenthesized matrices invertible
for $\eta>0$, one has
$(\bm A^T\bm A+\eta\bm I_{LN})^{-1}\bm A^T
=\bm A^T(\bm A\bm A^T+\eta\bm I_K)^{-1}$.   Applying this identity with $\bm A=\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+$ to the
   solution of the stationarity condition yields \eqref{eq:update}.

label: eq:lipschitz
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Tracking-error bound

label: eq:linear-residual
title: Proof
body_md:
Taylor's theorem gives
$\left\lVert \bm r_\theta(\Delta\bm\theta^\star)\right\rVert_2
\leq
\frac{\beta}{2}\left\lVert \Delta\bm\theta^\star\right\rVert_2^2$.
Moreover, from \eqref{eq:update},
 
\begin{equation}
\overline{\bm b}
+
\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+\Delta\bm\theta^\star
=
\eta
\left[
\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+
(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^T
+\eta\bm I_K
\right]^{-1}
\overline{\bm b}.
\label{eq:linear-residual}
\end{equation}
 
The result follows by the triangle inequality.
head: environment

label: eq:pseudo
title: Corollary
body_md:
If $\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+$ has full row rank (which requires
$LN\geq K$) and $\eta\rightarrow0$, then
 
\begin{equation}
\Delta\bm\theta^\star
=
-
(\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+)^\dagger
\overline{\bm b},
\quad
\overline{\bm b}
+
\overline{\bm J}_\theta^+\Delta\bm\theta^\star
=
\bm 0.
\label{eq:pseudo}
\end{equation}
 
Hence, the minimum-norm update cancels the linearized normalized SNR
mismatch exactly, leaving only a second-order phase-domain residual.
